extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners handling ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards for proposing, formatting, filing, and considering amendments to a patent specification, claims, drawings, and inventorship in ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings under 37 CFR and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of added specification paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 CFR 1.530(d)(1), all paragraphs which are added to the specification must be submitted as completely underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any paragraph added to the specification during reexamination must be presented with underlining throughout. Form paragraph guidance (e.g., MPEP form paragraphs) may be used to notify patent owner of this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full text of amended patent claims with markings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim is changed, the full text of any claim to be changed must be submitted with markings (underlining for additions, single brackets for deletions) as required by 37 CFR 1.530(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's amendments prepared when the NIRC is made also require full text with markings; the 37 CFR 1.121(g) exception for examiner's amendments does not apply in reexamination. Requirements apply regardless of paper or compact disc submission (37 CFR 1.96 or 1.825).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status must be set forth with amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 CFR 1.530(e), each amendment submitted must set forth the status of all patent claims and all added claims as of the date of the submission: whether the claim is pending or canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit claim status will generally result in an informal response notification to the patent owner prior to final rejection (see MPEP § 2266.02); an amendment submitted after final rejection that fails to set forth claim status will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of support for claim changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim amendment must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the amendment (support for changes, insertions and deletions) as required by 37 CFR 1.530(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit the explanation will generally result in a notification that the amendment is not completely responsive prior to final rejection (see MPEP § 2266.01). Amendments submitted after final rejection without explanation will not be entered. Patent owner should also point out what is changed in the 'Remarks' portion of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings convention for amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.530(f) identifies the type of markings required: underlining for added material and single brackets for material deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These markings show additions and deletions relative to the original patent text; when reexamination certificate is printed, underlined matter is printed in italics and brackets are printed as inserted in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original patent claim numbering cannot be renumbered
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.530(g) states that original patent claims may not be renumbered; a patent claim retains its number even if canceled in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering of any added claims must begin after the last original patent claim. A claim number previously assigned to a new claim that has been canceled should not be reassigned to a different new claim during the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: All changes are made vis-a-vis the original patent
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to the patent being reexamined must be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the date of the filing of the request for reexamination (37 CFR 1.530(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prior concluded post-patent proceeding changed the patent (prior reexamination certificate, reissue, certificate of correction), the first amendment must be made relative to the patent as changed by that prior proceeding; subsequent amendments must still be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the filing date of the reexamination request. Rare exceptions noted where concluded post-patent proceeding changes occur while reexamination pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendments to expired patents (except cancellation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.530(j), 'No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent.' If a patent expires during reexamination, all amendments to claims and all claims added during the proceeding are withdrawn; only cancellation of original patent claims is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At time of NIRC, examiner should ensure all rejected and objected claims are canceled; examiner may issue examiner’s amendment canceling such claims. Any amendment other than cancellation will not be incorporated into an expired patent by certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation format for changes to specification paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending the specification, submit a copy of the entire paragraph being amended with underlining and bracketing (i.e., present replacement paragraph with underlining/bracketing showing changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows replacement of a paragraph with underlined additions and bracketed deletions. Use complete paragraph text, not fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation format for amended original patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For changes to the patent claims, submit a copy of the entire patent claim with amendments shown by underlining and bracketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: indicate 'Claim 6. (amended)' then present full claim text with underlining and brackets marking changes versus the original patent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling when changing claim dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dependency of any original patent claim is to be changed by amendment, it is proper to make that original patent claim dependent upon a later-filed higher numbered claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow numbering and dependency conventions; do not renumber original claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of new claims (claims not in the patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed new claim should be presented with underlining throughout the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert new claim with underlining for the entire claim text. Numbering of added claims begins after the highest original claim number. If new claims are later canceled prior to issuance, examiner will renumber remaining new claims when preparing NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of a new claim previously presented
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of a new claim must present the entire text of the new claim containing the amendatory material, and it must be underlined throughout the claim; it cannot contain bracketing or other indication of what was in the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because changes are made vis-a-vis the original patent, the amended new claim shows only the changes from the original patent (underlined) and not any bracketed deletions from prior new-claim versions. Patent owner must point out what is changed in 'Remarks' and provide support explanation per 37 CFR 1.530(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple amendments to original patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one amendment is made to an original patent claim, each later amendment must include the changes previously presented as well as the new changes, presented relative to the original patent text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletions of words that were added in a prior amendment (and that never appeared in the original patent) are simply omitted in subsequent amendments (not bracketed). Newly added words are underlined; previously-added words that are now deleted are omitted (not bracketed) because they were never part of the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment format and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner; once approved, submit new sheets of drawings (in compliance with § 1.84) for each sheet changed. Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended', added figures as 'New', canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to original patent drawing sheets are not permitted; changes require substitute sheets. The sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes in red will be made part of the record. If approved but new sheets are not timely filed before NIRC, an ex parte Quayle action should set one-month SSP for filing; failure to file may result in issued certificate with drawings not reflecting proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the copy of patent drawings submitted with request
rubrics_metrics.description: The copy of the patent drawings submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.510(b)(4) will be used for reexamination purposes provided no change is made to the drawings. If there is any change, new sheets must be submitted and changes may NOT be made on original patent drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each changed drawing sheet requires a new sheet; do not annotate or alter the original patent drawing pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When it appears the correct inventor(s) were not named through error without deceptive intention, the Director may, on petition of all parties and satisfactory proof and fee under § 1.324, include an amendment naming only the actual inventor(s) in the reexamination certificate (37 CFR 1.530(l)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition to correct inventorship must satisfy § 1.324. If the reexamination concludes without issuing a reexamination certificate, a certificate of correction may be issued upon request (37 CFR 1.530(l)(2)), or correction may be pursued via reissue under 35 U.S.C. 251 (see MPEP § 1412.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees for claims added during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.20(c) establishes excess claims fees for: (c)(3) each independent claim in excess of three and in excess of the number of independent claims in the patent; (c)(4) each claim (dependent or independent) in excess of twenty and in excess of the number of claims in the patent being reexamined. Amounts differ for small vs other than small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees must be paid with the request or when claims are later presented; if not paid, fees must be paid or the claims canceled prior to expiration of the time set in a Notice of Fee Deficiency (PTOL-475) to avoid abandonment. Examples illustrate fee application. Effective for amendments filed on or after Dec 8, 2004. If unpaid, notice PTOL-475 with one-month SSP issued; extension possible under 37 CFR 1.550(c). Failure to pay may result in termination under 37 CFR 1.550(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation rules for excess claims fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent excess claims fee applies only if amendment increases independent claims above both three and the number of independent claims in the patent; the total excess claims fee applies only if amendment increases total claims above both twenty and the number of claims in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for a patent with six independent claims and thirty total claims demonstrate when no fee is due, when independent fee applies, when total fee applies, and when both apply depending on how many claims are canceled/added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and consideration of statements and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file or serve the documents set forth in §§ 1.530 (patent owner statement) or 1.535 (third party reply) may result in their being refused consideration; only submissions expressly provided in these sections will be considered prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely submissions will ordinarily not be considered and may not be placed of record (returned to sender) except limited circumstances for untimely patent owner papers. Any paper filed without required proof of service may be denied consideration; the clerk should inquire about service and, if none, place the paper in file but not consider it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party requester reply rules and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply by the ex parte reexamination requester to the patent owner’s statement under § 1.530 may be filed within two months from the date of service of the patent owner’s statement (35 U.S.C. 304 and 37 CFR 1.535).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must be served on the patent owner per § 1.248. No extensions of time will be granted. Reply may include additional prior art and raise any issue appropriate for reexamination; but if no patent owner statement is filed, no reply is permitted. The third party requester may not file further papers after this reply; any further papers will be returned and not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration by examiner of submissions and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Once reexamination is ordered, any submissions properly filed and served in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530 and 1.535 will be considered by the examiner when preparing the first Office action; examiner is guided by 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) for amendments and 1.530(c) for patent owner statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a requester’s reply raises issues not previously presented, the examiner will treat them in the Office action if within the scope of reexamination; issues not within scope should be handled pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c). For handling new matter, see MPEP § 2270.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of reexamination proceedings and limit on enlarging claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination will be conducted according to procedures for initial examination (sections 132 and 133). The patent owner may propose any amendment or new claim to distinguish the invention from cited prior art or to respond to adverse patentability decisions, but 'No proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim of the patent will be permitted in a reexamination proceeding' (35 U.S.C. 305).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings (including appeals) are to be conducted with special dispatch. See 37 CFR 1.550 for conduct of ex parte reexamination proceedings; result is issuance of an ex parte reexamination certificate under § 1.570.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of amendments submitted after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment submitted after final rejection that fails to comply with requirements (e.g., lacks claim status or explanatory support) will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph use: after final rejection such amendments should not be entered and patent owner informed by advisory Office action (PTOL-467). Informal amendments submitted after final rejection are treated as not entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical cross-references for related amendment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For clerical handling and special cases (merged proceedings; amendments where prior reexamination certificate or reissue exists; handling dependent claims), refer to specific MPEP sections (e.g., § 2270, § 2670, § 2283, § 2285, § 2295, § 2260.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an amendment is made in a pending reexamination where a prior certificate/reissue exists, italicized text of certificate/reissue is treated as if originally present and bracketed text treated as never present; present amendments accordingly (see MPEP § 2295/§ 2285 guidance).
